question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose a generic optional reset-correlation token through the agent-harness reset and plugin session-end contracts for plugins that need to pair a successful reset with a delayed lifecycle event?
rationale: The code path is focused and additive, but the PR establishes a shared plugin API contract rather than a Codex-private implementation detail; repository policy treats plugin API evolution as compatibility-sensitive and no explicit owner decision is present in the discussion.

options.title: Accept the generic lifecycle seam
options.body: Keep the optional token as a documented generic correlation mechanism, subject to a fresh current-main merge-head validation.

options.title: Keep the correlation private
options.body: Rework the reset-to-session-end association behind an owner-approved internal seam if maintainers do not want this plugin API commitment.

recommendation.title: Accept the generic lifecycle seam
recommendation.body: Keep the optional token as a documented generic correlation mechanism, subject to a fresh current-main merge-head validation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the retained-ID reset lifecycle that created the need for this follow-up and are best placed to confirm the intended shared reset contract.
